items.question: A retailer's pricing team runs an agent with a headless browser. In one workflow it visits competitor and marketplace pages; in another it reads the company's internal margin dashboard, which authenticates by session cookie. Both workflows currently share one browser profile so the agent does not have to re-authenticate. A reviewer flags the arrangement. What is the correct isolation design?

options.A: Keep one browser profile but clear cookies, local storage and session storage between navigations to external and internal origins, so no credential is present when an untrusted page loads.
options.B: Run untrusted browsing in an isolated browser context with no credentials and no network route to internal origins, passing only validated data across.
options.C: Restrict external browsing to a maintained allowlist of competitor and marketplace domains, refreshed by the pricing team, so the agent never visits an arbitrary site.
options.D: Use the browser's private-browsing mode for all agent sessions, so cookies and cached credentials are discarded and no state is retained between one run and the next.

items.question: A property-listings portal's assistant can return an owner's contact details to verified estate agents. Every individual lookup is legitimate and authorised. A risk review is concerned about an agent account retrieving thousands of owner records one at a time to build a marketing list. Which two controls address this? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Apply per-principal volume and velocity limits to the lookup tool, with alerting when a session's count of distinct records retrieved departs from normal working patterns.
options.B: Require the model to include a justification string with each lookup call, stored alongside the result so that the stated purpose is available for later review.
options.C: Return owner contact details only after a deterministic check that the requesting agent holds an active mandate on that specific property.
options.D: Add latency to repeated lookups within a session so that high-volume retrieval becomes impractically slow for anyone attempting to collect records in bulk.
options.E: Log every lookup with the calling agent, the record retrieved and a timestamp, and review those logs monthly for unusual patterns.

items.question: When is a separate classifier call preferable to expressing a content policy as instructions inside the main system prompt?

options.A: When the policy must hold independently of generation — versioned, measured and enforced even if the prompt or model changes.
options.B: When the policy has only a small number of rules, since short policies are easier to express as a standalone classification task.
options.C: When the latency budget is tight, since an additional classifier call completes faster than the extra tokens a longer system prompt would add.
options.D: When the policy changes rarely, since a classifier threshold is harder to update at short notice than a line of prompt text a developer can edit.

items.question: An agricultural co-operative runs an overnight reconciliation agent across grain-delivery, weighbridge and settlement systems. A single run lasts up to six hours, calls several services, and writes settlement adjustments in its final phase. Today it authenticates with one long-lived API key held in the secrets manager and loaded at start-up. How should credentials be handled instead?

options.A: Keep the long-lived key but rotate it on the organisation's standard quarterly schedule and restrict retrieval from the secrets manager to the batch host's own service identity.
options.B: Mint short-lived credentials scoped to the permissions of the current phase, refresh them from the orchestrator as the run progresses, and bind them to the run identity so they cannot be replayed.
options.C: Reuse the interactive settlement service's credential, since the same weighbridge and settlement operations are being performed and its permissions are already correct for them.
options.D: Keep one credential for the whole run but hold it encrypted in memory, decrypting it only at each call site so that the plaintext value exists for the shortest possible time during the six hours the job is active.

items.question: A media-monitoring agency runs an agent that loops up to twelve times per task: plan, retrieve from a news corpus, call summarisation and publication tools, then generate. Guardrails currently run once on the user's opening request and once on the final response. A reviewer notes that most of what the model reads and most of what it does happens between those two points. Where should guardrails sit?

options.A: At the start and end of the run only, since the intermediate planning, retrieval and tool steps are internal to the system and are never exposed to a user or to a publication channel.
options.B: On every model call in the loop, running the complete input and output guardrail stack at each of the twelve iterations, including the internal planning turns, so no step is left unchecked.
options.C: At each trust-boundary crossing: content entering from retrieval or tools is marked and screened, each proposed tool call is authorised against the caller's entitlements before it executes, and the final response is checked.
options.D: Only on tool calls, since generation that produces no side effect cannot cause harm outside the loop and the intermediate planning text is never shown to anyone, which makes screening it pure overhead on every iteration.

items.question: A rail operator's maintenance-planning agent takes four inputs: chat from authenticated engineers, sensor telemetry from the internal fleet platform, inspection reports uploaded by contractor firms, and free-text availability and substitution notes returned by a parts vendor's authenticated API. It can create work orders and place parts orders. The team's threat model marks only the contractor uploads as untrusted, on the grounds that the other three arrive over authenticated internal channels. What is the defect in that model?

options.A: Authentication of a channel says nothing about who authored the payload; the vendor's free-text notes are written outside the organisation and are untrusted on the same footing as the contractor uploads.
options.B: Engineer chat should also be marked untrusted, because an engineer's account can be phished or shared and the model has no way to detect that it is talking to an attacker rather than to staff.
options.C: The model is adequate as drawn, because telemetry readings and vendor API responses are machine-generated, and machine-generated data cannot carry instructions into the agent's context the way a human-written document can.
options.D: Trust boundaries should be drawn at the outputs rather than the inputs, so the model should mark the two write tools and the work-order schema instead of classifying the four input sources.

items.question: A veterinary poisons helpline runs an assistant for farm vets, who need concrete toxicology detail — agrochemical exposure thresholds, decontamination protocols, antidote dosing for livestock. The generic harmful-substances category in the guardrail stack blocks roughly a fifth of clinical questions. The helpline has a two-minute response commitment and every user authenticates against a professional register. How should the policy be adjusted?

options.A: Remove the harmful-substances category from this deployment entirely, since every authenticated user is a veterinary professional on a public register and the category blocks their core work.
options.B: Keep the generic category as configured and add a system-prompt instruction telling the assistant that clinical toxicology for livestock is in scope for this product and should be answered fully.
options.C: Redefine the category for this deployment: permit clinical toxicology where the session is bound to a verified professional account and the request matches an allowlisted clinical intent, and block otherwise.
options.D: Keep the generic block in place and route every blocked question to an on-call human toxicologist, so that no clinical need goes unanswered and the guardrail configuration stays identical to every other deployment the vendor ships.

items.question: A housing association's tenant portal assistant answers questions about rent, repairs and tenancy. A tenant emails a screenshot showing an arrears figure they say belongs to a neighbour. The support team cannot match that figure to any record in the system, and the neighbour's actual balance is different. The assistant serves 40,000 tenants. What should the team do next?

options.A: Disable the assistant for all tenants immediately and keep it down until root cause is established, on the basis that a suspected cross-tenant disclosure outranks availability for a service of this kind.
options.B: Reply to the tenant asking them to reproduce the behaviour and send further screenshots and timestamps, so the team can characterise the pattern before committing engineering time.
options.C: Notify the regulator of a suspected personal-data breach immediately, so the clock on the statutory reporting obligation starts from the earliest possible point rather than from confirmation.
options.D: Pull the request trace for that session and check whether any other tenant's record was present in the assembled context, since a retrieval-scoping defect and a fabricated figure demand different responses.

items.question: What distinguishes output sanitisation from output moderation in a Claude-based system?

options.A: Sanitisation runs on the response before it is rendered, whereas moderation runs on it after the user has already seen it and reported a problem through the support channel.
options.B: Sanitisation applies only to structured output such as JSON or generated code, while moderation applies only to the free-text responses that a human being will read.
options.C: Moderation decides whether the content is permissible for the recipient to receive; sanitisation makes the content safe for whatever system will interpret, render or execute it.
options.D: Moderation is performed by a model, while sanitisation is the same check run through a model a second time under a stricter prompt written by the safety team.

items.question: A B2B sales organisation's agent drafts and sends prospect emails. It reads CRM account records that include notes pasted from prospect correspondence and forwarded threads. Sends go to external recipients and cannot be recalled. Which three controls prevent or bound a bad send, rather than record one after the fact? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Blind-copy a monitoring mailbox on every message the agent sends, so that all outbound mail is retained centrally and available for review by the sales operations team.
options.B: Constrain recipients to addresses already present on the CRM record for the account in scope, resolved by the application rather than taken from the model's arguments.
options.C: Run the drafted body through an outbound content check for confidential markers, internal-only material and content belonging to other accounts before dispatch.
options.D: Hold sends in an outbox with a short delay and a per-user daily cap, so an anomalous burst can be stopped before any of it is delivered.
options.E: Instruct the agent in its system prompt never to include information drawn from other accounts in an email it drafts or sends.

items.question: A games studio's asset-pipeline agent reads and writes files while preparing builds. It runs on a shared build host that also holds signing material and other projects' working directories. The current guard checks that each requested path begins with the project directory before the file is opened. A security engineer says this is insufficient. What should replace it?

options.A: Keep the prefix check but also reject any path containing a parent-directory segment, normalising duplicate separators first, before comparing the string to the project directory.
options.B: Run the agent process as an operating-system user whose home directory is the project directory, so that anything it opens without an absolute path resolves inside the project rather than elsewhere on the build host.
options.C: Log every file operation with its fully resolved path and raise an alert to the build on-call team whenever a write lands outside the project directory on the shared build host.
options.D: Canonicalise each requested path, resolving links and relative segments, before checking it against an allowlist of roots; mount only those roots into the container and separate read-only from writable.

items.question: An interactive-fiction app lets users create characters and play out long collaborative stories; adopting a persona is the entire product. Safety analysis finds sessions where the fictional frame was used to move the exchange toward content the app must not produce, with the character's established voice cited as justification for continuing. The team cannot restrict roleplay itself. How should policy be enforced?

options.A: Detect and decline requests that ask the assistant to adopt, maintain or return to a named character, since the persona framing is the vector the flagged sessions exploited.
options.B: Enforce policy with guardrails that score the content of the exchange independently of the fictional frame, so a character's voice may vary while the set of permitted content does not.
options.C: Re-inject the full safety rules into the system prompt before every turn, so that an established character cannot gradually displace them as the story context grows over a long session.
options.D: Allow only personas drawn from a curated library the studio authors and reviews each release, rather than the free-form personas users currently write for themselves without oversight.

items.question: A payments company is implementing a guardrail stack and must decide, per check, between a deterministic implementation and a model-based one. Which two of the following checks are correctly matched to a deterministic implementation? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Detecting coercive or abusive language in an inbound message, using a maintained keyword and phrase list.
options.B: Detecting card numbers and IBANs in outbound text, using pattern matching with checksum validation.
options.C: Judging whether a refusal was phrased with adequate empathy, using a template similarity match.
options.D: Verifying that a payee IBAN in a proposed transfer appears on the customer's saved-payee list, using a direct lookup against that list.
options.E: Identifying attempts to obtain another customer's balance, using regular expressions over the request text.

items.question: A benefits agency's assistant runs three safety layers: an input classifier, an output classifier, and an independent intent check on proposed actions. Together they now cost more per request than the generation itself, and the programme's annual budget is fixed and already committed. The safety lead is asked to reduce guardrail spend by roughly a third without an unmeasured loss of coverage. What should be done first?

options.A: Move all three layers to the cheapest model tier, keeping the architecture intact and accepting a uniform reduction in classifier quality across the whole stack.
options.B: Remove the output classifier, since the input classifier and the intent check both act earlier in the request path and prevention is preferable to detection.
options.C: Measure each layer's unique contribution on held-out traffic and remove or narrow the layer with the least unique coverage.
options.D: Run the full stack on a sampled 20% of traffic and the input classifier alone on the remainder, which reduces spend by roughly the required amount without removing any layer entirely.

items.question: An IT service-management platform runs two agents. The first triages inbound customer emails and writes a summary note onto the ticket. The second, running later, reads the ticket's full history — including those notes — to propose and execute runbook steps. Investigation of an unexplained runbook execution finds that text originating in a customer's email was carried into the triage note and then read by the second agent as internal record. What change addresses this class of failure?

options.A: Store every persisted item with its author and a derived trust level, and have downstream consumers apply untrusted-content handling to anything not authored by an authenticated human.
options.B: Have the triage agent sanitise its notes by removing instruction-like language before writing them to the ticket, so that nothing imperative is ever persisted into the ticket history.
options.C: Restrict the second agent to ticket history from the last 24 hours, so that older accumulated notes and correspondence cannot influence the runbook steps it proposes.
options.D: Have the second agent read the customer's original email directly rather than the triage agent's summary note, removing the intermediate step that lost the content's origin.

items.question: A fitness app's coaching assistant keeps context across sessions by persisting the complete transcript of every conversation indefinitely. Transcripts include injury history, medication mentions and body-composition figures that users volunteer. Only a small set of facts — goals, physical constraints and training preferences — is actually used to personalise later sessions. What should the team change?

options.A: Continue persisting full transcripts but encrypt them at rest under a key held separately for each user account, so a storage compromise yields nothing.
options.B: Persist a structured state summary of the fields later sessions use, and keep raw turns only for the active session.
options.C: Continue persisting full transcripts but exclude any turn the user has explicitly flagged as private using the in-chat privacy control before sending it.
options.D: Continue persisting full transcripts and compress the older ones, so that storage growth stays under control as coaching history accumulates across the whole user base.

items.question: A construction firm's assistant indexes site reports uploaded by supervisors: PDFs with embedded photographs, standalone images of handwritten sheets, and spreadsheets. The current ingestion path extracts document body text and runs it through an injection screen before indexing. A reviewer points out that a meaningful share of the content the model eventually reads never passes through that screen. What should ingestion do?

options.A: Continue screening extracted body text and skip the image paths, since site photographs and scans of handwritten sheets are pixels rather than instructions the model could act on.
options.B: Convert every upload to PDF at ingestion so that a single parser and a single screen cover all formats, removing the per-format branching that currently lets some content bypass the check at ingestion time.
options.C: Accept uploads only from supervisors whose accounts have been verified against the staff directory and re-verified each quarter, so the origin of every indexed document is known before it enters the corpus.
options.D: Normalise every upload to a canonical text representation — including text recognised in images, document metadata and hidden layers — and screen and provenance-mark that representation before indexing.

items.question: A warehouse automation vendor lets an agent dispatch put-away tasks and re-route conveyor jobs. Some commands move heavy loads and cannot be undone by a subsequent command once the equipment has acted. Which two controls address the irreversibility specifically? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Log every dispatched command with its complete parameter set and timestamp, so any incident can be reconstructed precisely.
options.B: Require that commands reaching the control system be selected from a pre-approved operation set, with parameters bounded by a physical envelope enforced in the controller itself rather than in the agent.
options.C: Run the agent on the higher-capability model tier for any command affecting physical equipment.
options.D: Require a second human to confirm any command that cannot be undone by a later command.
options.E: Present a confirmation prompt to the floor operator for every command the agent issues, whatever its effect.

items.question: A marketing automation platform's agent can create scheduled jobs — recurring campaign sends, list refreshes, report deliveries — that execute later under the agent's own service identity, after the originating session has ended. Scheduled sends are a core product capability. A security review notes that a job created during one session keeps running with no connection to the person who asked for it or to the entitlements they held. What is the correct design?

options.A: Bind each created job to the requesting person's identity with an explicit expiry, re-evaluate that person's entitlements at every execution, and treat schedule creation as a gated action in its own right.
options.B: Allow schedule creation but cap the number of jobs any single session may create, limiting how much recurring work can be established in one interaction with the agent.
options.C: Allow the agent to create only read-only jobs such as report deliveries and list refreshes, and require a marketing operations user to configure by hand any job that sends.
options.D: Delete all agent-created jobs nightly and require them to be recreated in a subsequent session, so that no schedule persists beyond a single day without someone deliberately establishing it again the following morning.

items.question: A team is worried that users may induce their assistant to reveal its system prompt. What is the correct architectural posture?

options.A: Add explicit non-disclosure instructions and a canary check that blocks any response containing a marker string from the prompt, treating those as the control.
options.B: Move the instructions out of the system role and into the first user turn of each conversation, so there is no system prompt in the request for the assistant to disclose.
options.C: Assume the prompt is discoverable and keep secrets, credentials and authorisation logic out of it; disclosure then costs confidentiality, not security.
options.D: Encrypt the system prompt at rest and in transit under a key held in the secrets manager, so its contents cannot be read even if the assistant reproduces parts of it.

items.question: A roadside-assistance provider is adding a voice assistant to its emergency line. The channel supports barge-in and the team's turn budget is under one second end to end. Transcription is imperfect, especially on short utterances and at motorway noise levels. The agent can dispatch a recovery vehicle. The web channel's input-plus-output classifier stack cannot fit inside the budget. Where should the enforceable controls go?

options.A: Apply the same input and output classifier stack the web channel uses and accept the additional round-trip latency, since safety cannot be traded for speed on an emergency line.
options.B: Classify only the transcript before the model call, since blocking at the earliest possible point saves the most time within a turn budget of under one second end to end.
options.C: Record all calls and have a quality team review flagged ones after the fact, since a live emergency conversation cannot accommodate synchronous controls at this budget.
options.D: Gate the generated response before speech synthesis and gate every dispatch against the caller's verified account, treating the transcript check as advisory.

items.question: An engineering company's internal knowledge assistant auto-publishes its answers as draft articles into the same wiki it retrieves from, on the theory that good answers should become reusable documentation. An engineer reports that a wrong configuration instruction now appears in three published drafts and is cited by the assistant as documented practice. Roughly 4,000 auto-published drafts exist. What should the team do next?

options.A: Add a verification pass in which the assistant checks each draft against the wiki before publication, and republish the existing drafts through it.
options.B: Halt auto-publication into the retrieval index, flag the existing auto-published drafts as unverified, and exclude them from retrieval until they have been reviewed.
options.C: Adjust retrieval ranking so that human-authored wiki pages consistently outrank auto-published drafts, keeping reviewed material at the top of every result set.
options.D: Expand the corpus with additional external documentation, so that the contaminated drafts carry proportionally less weight in retrieval across the whole index.

items.question: A transport ticketing operator is preparing to enable an agent that can issue refunds, amend bookings and cancel travel passes. The safety architect is defining which safety properties must be demonstrable — not merely described — before the write tools are switched on. Which three belong on that list? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: That the agent meets its target task-success rate on the golden evaluation set for refund and amendment scenarios.
options.B: That every write tool's authorisation is evaluated against the end user's identity, shown by a test in which a low-privilege user's request is rejected at the tool layer.
options.C: That untrusted content reaching the agent cannot cause a write without an independent check, shown by injection cases that live in the regression suite and run on every release.
options.D: That the safety team has reviewed the system prompt and confirmed it contains an explicit refusal instruction for each policy category.
options.E: That the guardrail stack's false-positive and false-negative rates have been measured on production-like traffic, with the thresholds in force recorded.

items.question: A Nordic energy retailer is launching a Claude-based billing assistant for its 1.8 million domestic customers. The assistant answers questions about the customer's own consumption and invoices, and the team also wants to retain transcripts for six months to tune prompts. The DPO must record a lawful basis before go-live. The product manager argues that consent should be collected on first use because 'consent is always the safest option'. Which analysis should the architect support?

options.A: Basis follows purpose, not tooling: a query about the customer's own bill sits under the basis recorded for servicing the supply contract, while retaining transcripts to tune prompts is a separate purpose with its own basis and record entry.
options.B: Consent must be captured on first use through a dialog the customer accepts before the chat opens, because introducing a new processing technology into an existing service resets the basis for the whole interaction.
options.C: No fresh assessment is required, because the model provider acts as a processor under a data processing agreement and the retailer's existing basis for the billing relationship therefore extends to everything the assistant does with the data.
options.D: A single legitimate interests assessment should cover the assistant end to end, with one balancing test carrying both the service-delivery use and the six-month transcript retention as a single entry in the processing record.

items.question: A German insurtech runs a Claude assistant over customer correspondence. The architecture holds: the source correspondence in a document store, chunk text plus embeddings in a vector index, a prompt cache keyed on rendered context, ninety days of request and response payloads in a third-party observability platform, and a weekly frozen evaluation snapshot sampled from real traffic. A customer submits an erasure request that the legal team has confirmed is valid. What should the architect implement?

options.A: Delete the source correspondence from the document store and let the next scheduled full index rebuild remove the derived vectors and chunk text, since embeddings are numerical derivations rather than personal data in their own right.
options.B: Remove the customer's name, policy number and contact details from the stored transcripts, which renders the remaining free text anonymous and therefore places it outside the scope of the request.
options.C: Delete or re-derive that customer's data in every derived store - index chunks, cached prompts, retained logs and the evaluation snapshot - on a documented internal deadline, with backups handled by restore-time re-deletion.
options.D: Hold the request and record that the firm's immutable decision log carries an overriding retention obligation, so no copy of the customer's data anywhere in the platform can be removed while that log exists.

items.question: Under GDPR, what most directly determines whether a data protection impact assessment is required before an organisation deploys an LLM-based feature?

options.A: Whether any personal data will leave the European Economic Area during inference, prompt caching or trace storage.
options.B: Whether the model provider is engaged under contract as a processor rather than as an independent controller.
options.C: Whether the volume of personal data processed exceeds the organisation's own internal materiality threshold.
options.D: Whether the processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals, given its nature and scope.

items.question: A UK motor insurer must be able to reconstruct any automated claim-triage recommendation its Claude-based system produced, for the whole regulatory retention window. Today the platform stores the model's final output text and a timestamp against the claim reference. Which TWO additions do most to make a past recommendation genuinely reconstructible? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: A monthly aggregate report of triage outcomes broken down by product line, region and claim value band.
options.B: The exact rendered prompt sent to the model, including the retrieved policy and claim documents and each document's version identifier.
options.C: A natural-language rationale that the model is asked to emit alongside each recommendation, explaining why it reached its conclusion.
options.D: The resolved model identifier and version, together with the temperature and other decoding parameters used for that call.
options.E: The name of the claims handler in every case where a human overrode the system's recommendation, with the date of the override.

items.question: A Dutch consumer lender receives a request from its supervisory authority to reproduce the Claude-generated affordability summary that supported a specific credit decision made twenty-six months ago. The platform archives full request and response payloads to object storage. However, prompts are assembled at runtime from a template repository that has changed roughly forty times since, and the deployment used a model alias that has been repointed twice. The team has three weeks to respond. What should the architect do first?

options.A: Re-run the archived inputs against the current production configuration and submit the resulting output as the reproduction, noting in the covering letter that generation is non-deterministic.
options.B: Inspect the archived payload for that request to establish whether it holds the fully rendered prompt and the resolved model version, since if it does the archive is itself the evidence.
options.C: Check out the template repository at the commit tagged nearest the decision date, rebuild the prompt from that template and the stored variable values, and submit the rebuilt prompt as the reproduction.
options.D: Open a support case asking the model provider to retrieve the original completion from its own side, so the response can be corroborated by an independent party.

items.question: A prospective enterprise customer asks for a SOC 2 Type II report covering your Claude-based platform rather than the Type I you already hold. What distinguishes the two?

options.A: A Type II examines whether controls operated effectively across a review period, while a Type I examines design suitability at a point in time.
options.B: A Type II report covers all five trust services criteria, while a Type I covers only the security criterion and its common controls.
options.C: A Type II report is issued by an independent audit firm, while a Type I is a self-assessment questionnaire published by the service organisation.
options.D: A Type II report extends the assessment to the organisation's subprocessors, while a Type I covers only systems the organisation operates itself.

items.question: A travel booking platform wants a Claude agent to help support staff resolve payment disputes. The agent would read the booking record, the payment attempt history and the customer's message. Full primary account numbers currently appear in the payment attempt records. All prompts and completions pass through an internal model gateway and are written to a shared transcript store and a third-party tracing service, neither of which is segmented from the rest of the estate. The security architect must decide how to proceed before build starts.

options.A: Encrypt the transcript store and the tracing pipeline at rest with customer-managed keys, restrict access to a named support role, and treat those controls as removing both systems from cardholder data environment scope.
options.B: Add a system prompt rule instructing the model never to repeat a card number in its output, and monitor completions with an automated detector that redacts any match before it reaches the agent.
options.C: Accept the gateway, transcript store and tracing service into the cardholder data environment and complete the full assessment for all three, since any component supporting a payment workflow is in scope regardless of design.
options.D: Keep primary account numbers out of the prompt by passing a token that only an existing in-scope service can resolve, so the gateway, transcript store and tracing service never hold cardholder data.

items.question: A pan-EU logistics group has two Claude-based tools nearing launch. The first ranks applicants for warehouse roles and surfaces a shortlist; a recruiter reviews every ranking and no candidate is rejected without a human clicking through. The second summarises supplier contracts for the in-house legal team. The general counsel argues that because a recruiter is always in the loop, the shortlisting tool avoids the heavier obligations under the EU AI Act. How should the architect frame the classification?

options.A: Because a recruiter reviews every ranking and no candidate is rejected without a human clicking through, the shortlisting tool falls outside the high-risk tier and owes only the transparency duties.
options.B: Classification follows the system's intended purpose, so a tool used to select candidates for employment sits in the high-risk tier; effective human oversight is an obligation that tier imposes, not an exit from it.
options.C: The contract summarisation tool carries the higher regulatory risk of the two, because it processes commercially sensitive third-party information and its errors can bind the company.
options.D: Risk tier is determined by the capability of the underlying general-purpose model, so the obligations sit with the model provider and the logistics group inherits them through its contract.

items.question: An organisation deploys a customer-facing Claude assistant to EU users. Which obligation attaches primarily because the system interacts directly with natural persons, rather than because of the risk tier its use case falls into?

options.A: A conformity assessment against the applicable requirements must be completed before the system is put into service.
options.B: The system must be entered in the relevant EU database before it is placed on the market or put into service.
options.C: People must be informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless that is obvious in the circumstances.
options.D: A post-market monitoring plan must be maintained, with serious incidents reported to the market surveillance authority.

items.question: A US regional bank must put its Claude-based commercial-loan memo drafting and covenant-risk flagging system through independent validation before it can leave pilot, under a model risk management framework of the SR 11-7 type. The model risk team is scoping the engagement. Which THREE activities are core to that validation? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Obtaining sign-off from the development team lead confirming that the unit and integration test suites pass and the deployment pipeline is green.
options.B: Evaluating conceptual soundness: whether the design, prompt logic, retrieval sources and data suit the stated business purpose, with known limitations documented.
options.C: Establishing ongoing monitoring with defined performance thresholds, drift indicators and an escalation path once the system is live.
options.D: Negotiating commercial terms, capacity headroom and an uptime service level with the model provider before the system is approved for production.
options.E: Performing outcomes analysis, comparing system output against realised results or a benchmarked alternative on a held-out sample of loans.

items.question: A US telehealth provider generates clinical visit notes with Claude. The pipeline sends the visit transcript to the model provider, emits full request and response traces to a third-party observability vendor for latency debugging, and sends a weekly ten-percent sample of generated notes to an external clinical reviewer who scores accuracy under contract. Compliance is reviewing the arrangement before scale-up. What should the architect conclude?

options.A: Only the model provider requires a business associate agreement, since it is the only vendor performing a clinical function on the record rather than a supporting engineering one.
options.B: The observability vendor falls outside the requirement provided traces are sampled below a low threshold and are purged on a short retention clock enforced by the platform.
options.C: All three vendors - the model provider, the observability vendor and the scoring contractor - receive protected health information, so each needs its own business associate agreement and only the minimum data its function requires.
options.D: A business associate agreement with the model provider, combined with a flow-down clause obliging it to bind its own subcontractors and downstream processors, covers the full chain of vendors in this pipeline without separate agreements.

items.question: In a HIPAA-regulated Claude deployment, what does the minimum necessary standard most directly constrain about how prompts are built?

options.A: The amount of protected health information placed in each request must be limited to what that request's specific purpose needs.
options.B: Protected health information must be encrypted in transit and at rest wherever prompts are stored or transmitted.
options.C: Patient authorisation must be obtained before any protected health information is sent to an external vendor for processing.
options.D: Protected health information must be de-identified before it can be processed by any automated system, including a model endpoint.

items.question: A US credit union runs a Claude step that reads an application file, summarises it for the underwriter, and drafts a fluent paragraph explaining why the application looks weak. The actual approve or decline outcome is produced by a separate deterministic scorecard plus policy rules. Product proposes sending the model's paragraph to declined applicants as the adverse action notice, arguing it is clearer than the current reason codes. What position should the architect take?

options.A: The paragraph may be sent as written provided an underwriter reads and initials it before dispatch, since documented human review satisfies the accuracy requirement.
options.B: The disclosed reasons must come from the factors that actually drove the scorecard and rules outcome; the model may re-render a derived reason in plainer language but cannot be its source.
options.C: Having the model select from a fixed taxonomy of compliance-approved reason codes resolves the problem, because the wording of every code has already been reviewed.
options.D: The requirement is met by disclosing in the notice which model and version produced the assessment, together with an offer to explain the decision further on request.

items.question: A Swiss private bank has negotiated a zero-retention arrangement with its model provider: no prompt or completion is persisted on the provider side beyond the life of the request. The head of technology risk asks the architect what this changes about the design of the surrounding platform. What is the most important consequence?

options.A: Because nothing is retained by the provider, the bank no longer needs its own retention schedule for AI interactions and can fold them into its general records policy.
options.B: Because no copy persists at the provider, the interaction data is effectively anonymous once the response is returned, so subject access and erasure rights no longer attach to it.
options.C: Every artefact the bank may later need - incident forensics, abuse investigation, evaluation corpora, regulatory evidence - must now be captured and protected on the bank's own side.
options.D: Because the data never persists outside the request, cross-border transfer analysis for the inference call becomes unnecessary and the destination need not appear in the transfer register.

items.question: A Brazilian retail group's German subsidiary runs a Claude-based product-advice assistant for EU shoppers. Capacity in the current in-region deployment is tight ahead of a seasonal peak eight weeks away, and the platform team proposes repointing a share of traffic to a non-EEA region where headroom exists. The subsidiary's DPO has flagged the change as a cross-border transfer. What should the architect do first?

options.A: Test whether in-region capacity can be expanded to cover the peak, since removing the transfer costs less than justifying one; only if it cannot should a transfer mechanism and assessment be completed first.
options.B: Repoint the traffic now to protect the peak, and add the new destination region to the record of processing activities and the customer privacy notice at the next quarterly governance review.
options.C: Pseudonymise customer identifiers in the prompt by replacing the customer number with a lookup token before transmission, so the transferred payload is no longer personal data and the transfer question does not arise.
options.D: Adopt the model provider's published certifications for the destination region as the transfer mechanism, on the basis that the provider has already addressed the destination's legal environment.

items.question: An AI decision log must let an auditor demonstrate, after the fact, that no entry was altered or silently removed. Which property most directly provides that?

options.A: Write access to the log is restricted to a small group of platform operators authenticated with hardware security tokens.
options.B: Each record is sealed with a hash covering the preceding record, so alteration or deletion breaks a chain an auditor can recompute.
options.C: The log is replicated synchronously across three availability zones with automatic failover and periodic restore testing.
options.D: Records are written asynchronously through a durable queue, so an application failure can never block or drop entries on the logging path.

items.question: A media company's Claude-based content moderation system stores the prompt, retrieved policy context and decision for every review, and a nightly job deletes those records after thirty days under the published retention schedule. Litigation has now been filed and counsel has issued a preservation hold covering moderation decisions for a specific set of eleven creator accounts, going forward and back. The platform team must respond this week. What should the architect implement?

options.A: Suspend the expiry job across the entire corpus until the matter concludes, since selective suspension risks missing responsive records and creating spoliation exposure.
options.B: Let the nightly schedule continue to run, on the basis that consistent application of a published retention policy is itself the defence to a preservation challenge.
options.C: Add a per-record hold attribute that the expiry job checks before deleting, so records for the eleven accounts are preserved indefinitely while the rest of the corpus ages out on schedule.
options.D: Export a summary spreadsheet of the affected moderation outcomes to a separate legal archive and allow the primary records to expire, treating the export as the preserved copy.

items.question: A Spanish telco wants to build a permanent regression evaluation set from real customer-service transcripts handled by its Claude assistant, so that prompt changes can be gated on realistic cases. Privacy counsel has raised purpose limitation: the transcripts were collected to service customers, not to test software. Which TWO steps most directly address that objection? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Encrypt the evaluation store with customer-managed keys held in the telco's own key management service and rotate them on a fixed schedule.
options.B: Record a compatibility assessment for the secondary use, or establish a separate basis for it, and reflect the evaluation purpose in the processing record and the privacy notice.
options.C: Keep the evaluation set inside the production transcript database under the same retention clock, so that the secondary use inherits the primary purpose and needs no separate governance.
options.D: Obtain fresh explicit consent from every customer whose transcript is selected, since consent is the only basis that can support a secondary use of data already collected.
options.E: Reduce the corpus to the minimum number of cases needed for coverage and strip direct identifiers and irrelevant content from each transcript before it enters the evaluation store.

items.question: A French mobility platform uses a Claude-based pipeline to flag driver accounts for suspected fraud and deactivate them, which removes the driver's ability to earn on the platform. An operations agent sees a queue of flagged accounts and clicks confirm; the team measures the queue at roughly two hundred confirmations per agent per hour and the confirmation rate is 99.4 percent. Legal asks whether the GDPR safeguards for solely automated decisions apply. What should the architect advise?

options.A: Because an operations agent reviews the queue and confirms every deactivation before it takes effect, the decision is not solely automated, so the additional safeguards for such decisions do not attach here.
options.B: The safeguards are avoided by describing the pipeline's output as a recommendation in the internal documentation, the audit trail and the message shown to the driver.
options.C: A human step only removes the solely automated character if the reviewer has the information, authority and realistic time to reach a different conclusion; a queue confirmed at this rate does not.
options.D: The safeguards apply only where a model is the sole input; because a rules engine also contributes fraud signals, the decision is a hybrid and falls outside the regime.

items.question: An Australian workforce-management SaaS vendor embeds Claude in its scheduling product and serves EU customers under agreements naming the vendor as a processor. The product team now wants to mine customer prompt and response data across all tenants to improve a shared prompt library and to publish anonymised industry benchmarks. The vendor's counsel asks the architect for the correct characterisation before the feature is built.

options.A: Using tenant data for the vendor's own product improvement makes the vendor a controller for it, needing its own basis and transparency and permission in the customer agreements.
options.B: Because the agreements name the vendor as a processor, its role is contractually settled, and cross-tenant improvement work falls within the customer's documented processing instructions.
options.C: The vendor remains a processor because the data never leaves the infrastructure the customer's subscription pays for and is never disclosed to a fourth party or to another tenant.
options.D: The vendor remains a processor as long as the improvement work publishes only aggregated statistics, since aggregation removes both the benchmark and the underlying processing from scope.

items.question: A UK digital bank receives a subject access request from a customer covering everything the bank holds about them. Its Claude-based support assistant logs the customer's own messages, the assistant's replies, the retrieved documents used for each reply, a derived churn-risk score written back to the CRM, and the system prompt template. Some conversations concern a joint account and contain messages from the other account holder. What should the bank provide?

options.A: Refuse the conversational element on the basis that assistant logs are transient operational telemetry rather than a structured filing system, and answer from the core banking record and payment history only.
options.B: Export the full raw conversation log without redaction, including the other account holder's messages, since partial disclosure risks an incomplete and therefore non-compliant response.
options.C: Provide a summary of the topics the customer discussed and the dates of each conversation, since the assistant's replies are model-generated content rather than personal data about the requester.
options.D: Provide the requester's personal data in the logs - their messages, the replies about them and derived attributes such as the churn-risk score - with the other account holder's identifying information redacted.

items.question: A hospital wants to build an evaluation corpus from real clinical notes. Which statement correctly characterises HIPAA's two recognised de-identification routes?

options.A: Both routes require sign-off from a qualified statistician; they differ only in whether dates of service and geographic detail may be retained in the released corpus.
options.B: One route removes a listed set of identifiers with no actual knowledge of residual identifiability; the other rests on a documented expert determination of very small risk.
options.C: Either route still requires a business associate agreement before the resulting corpus can be shared with an external annotation or scoring vendor of any kind.
options.D: Both routes are satisfied by removing patient names and medical record numbers from the note text before the evaluation corpus is stored for reuse.

items.question: A healthcare analytics firm is onboarding a third-party AI observability vendor that will receive request and response traces from its Claude pipeline. Procurement has obtained the vendor's SOC 2 Type II report for a twelve-month period, and the opinion is unqualified with no exceptions noted. The architect is asked to sign off on the technical due diligence. What matters most in how the report is used?

options.A: Confirming the report covers all five trust services criteria, since anything narrower cannot support a regulated healthcare workload that touches patient data.
options.B: Treating the unqualified opinion as completing the firm's technical due diligence and filing the report as evidence for the firm's own next audit.
options.C: Working through the complementary user entity controls the report relies on, since the vendor's conclusions are conditional on the firm performing those controls itself.
options.D: Checking that the observation period ended within the last month, since a report covering an older period cannot be relied on for a current onboarding decision of this kind.

items.question: A Belgian medtech distributor licenses a third party's AI triage component, wraps it in its own interface, fine-tunes it on its own clinical dataset, defines the clinical intended purpose, and sells the result to EU clinics under its own brand. The distributor's regulatory lead has scoped the programme against the EU AI Act as a deployer obligation set. The architect is reviewing that scoping before the build is funded. What should be raised?

options.A: Branding the system as its own, defining the clinical intended purpose and substantially modifying the component can move the distributor into the provider role for that system.
options.B: Because a third party built the underlying model, provider obligations stay with that third party regardless of the branding, fine-tuning or intended purpose the distributor applies.
options.C: Obligations follow the hosting location, so keeping inference and fine-tuning within an EU region leaves the distributor with the lighter obligation set even after modification.
options.D: Because the system only suggests a triage category and a clinician makes the final call, the distributor's duties are limited to informing users that an AI system is involved.

items.question: A Canadian bank's model risk policy requires assessment and, where material, independent re-validation before any model change reaches production. Its Claude-based commercial credit memo assistant is validated and live. The product team ships prompt template edits and retrieval corpus updates roughly weekly, and has been treating them as configuration outside the policy. Model risk has now challenged this. What position should the architect take?

options.A: Prompt templates and retrieval corpora are configuration rather than model components, so the weekly release train can continue outside the change policy provided the model version is pinned.
options.B: Every prompt edit requires full independent re-validation before release, because any change that can alter model behaviour is by definition a material change to the model.
options.C: The policy should be read as applying only when the underlying model version changes, since that is the one component whose behaviour the bank neither controls nor tests itself.
options.D: Prompts, retrieval corpora and tool configuration are model components; triage each change against defined materiality criteria, with full re-validation reserved for material ones.

items.question: A national rail operator's Claude-based incident triage system writes a decision log that safety investigators rely on after the fact. The threat the safety board is most concerned about is a privileged internal user altering or removing entries to obscure a bad decision. Which TWO controls most directly address that specific threat? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Extending the log's retention period from three years to ten to match the longest applicable investigation window for rail incidents.
options.B: Compressing and tiering older log segments to cold object storage so the cost of the longer retention stays within the safety programme's budget.
options.C: Separating the ability to write log entries from the ability to administer the log store, so no single role can both produce and modify records.
options.D: Periodically anchoring a digest of the log with a party under different administrative control, so a coordinated internal rewrite becomes detectable.
options.E: Co-locating the log with the application's operational tables so that log writes and business writes commit in a single database transaction.

items.question: A Polish e-commerce company discovers that a debug endpoint on its Claude gateway was reachable without authentication for roughly six hours. The endpoint returned recent prompt payloads containing customer names, delivery addresses and order histories. The endpoint has already been disabled. Web server access logs show forty-one requests from three IP addresses outside the company's ranges, and those logs roll over on a seven-day cycle. The privacy office has been informed. What should the architect do next?

options.A: Notify every customer with an order placed in the exposure window immediately, on the basis that over-notification is always the safer course while the facts are still incomplete.
options.B: Preserve the access logs and the gateway's payload buffers out of the rotation and reconstruct which payloads were returned to each external request, before the seven-day window closes.
options.C: Rotate the gateway credentials, redeploy the service, and monitor for further anomalous requests from those three addresses for a week before deciding whether anything was actually taken.
options.D: Ask the model provider whether it retained copies of the affected prompts, so its records can be used to establish which payloads reached the three external addresses.

items.question: A team replaces customer identifiers with random tokens in its stored prompt archive and concludes the archive is now outside GDPR. What is the correct characterisation?

options.A: It is pseudonymisation, which keeps the data in scope, because re-identification remains possible and the remaining text may identify people.
options.B: It is anonymisation, because the random tokens cannot be reversed without access to the mapping table held by the platform team.
options.C: It is anonymisation provided the mapping table is held by a different team under separate access control and audit.
options.D: It is neither; masking identifier fields has no recognised status in the framework and therefore no effect on the archive's regulatory position.

items.question: A US personal-lines insurer uses Claude to extract structured features from free-text application narratives - property condition, occupation detail, prior loss circumstances - which then feed a conventional underwriting model. A state regulator asks how the insurer satisfies itself that these extracted features do not operate as proxies for protected characteristics. The chief actuary notes that no protected characteristic is present anywhere in the prompt or the feature set. What should the insurer's answer rest on?

options.A: Demonstrating that no protected characteristic appears in the prompt, the extracted features or the underwriting model, which establishes that no proxy effect can arise in pricing.
options.B: Evidencing a system prompt instruction that directs the model to disregard any protected characteristic mentioned in the narrative, together with monitoring for instruction violations.
options.C: Testing the extracted features for association with protected characteristics and testing outcomes for disparate impact on a held-out sample, retaining the feature dictionary and analyses as evidence.
options.D: Citing the model provider's published fairness evaluations for the base model, supplemented by the insurer's own accuracy testing of the extraction step against manual review.

items.question: A pharmaceutical company is launching a Claude-based medical information assistant for patients and healthcare professionals asking about its marketed products. Pharmacovigilance points out that if a user describes a suspected adverse reaction during a conversation, the company has received that information and its reporting obligations engage from that point. The assistant handles an expected several thousand conversations a day. What must the architecture do?

options.A: Display a prominent notice at the start of every conversation telling users not to report adverse events through this channel, which keeps the assistant outside pharmacovigilance scope.
options.B: Detect potential adverse event content in the conversation and route it to the safety case management system with the timestamp of first receipt, whatever channel it arrived through.
options.C: Have the model classify severity and close out non-serious reports itself with a templated acknowledgement, escalating only the cases it judges serious to the safety team.
options.D: Retain conversation transcripts for the standard period so the safety team can sweep them for reportable content during each periodic reporting cycle.

items.question: A city transport authority uses a Claude assistant to help officers draft replies to resident correspondence. A journalist files a public records request for all AI prompts and outputs relating to the tram extension consultation over the past year. The communications director wants to refuse on the basis that prompts are working drafts. The authority has a statutory response deadline. What should the architect do first?

options.A: Support the refusal on the basis that prompts are internal drafting aids rather than records of the authority, and confine the response to the correspondence actually sent to residents.
options.B: Produce a full export of the assistant's logs for the relevant period with resident names redacted, to demonstrate transparency and close the request within the deadline.
options.C: Ask the model provider to certify what it holds relating to the authority's account, so the response can account for any records held on the authority's behalf.
options.D: Establish which prompts, retrieved documents and outputs exist, where they are held and which contain residents' personal data, before any release or refusal position is taken.

items.question: A broker-dealer's client-facing advisers use a Claude assistant inside their desktop to ask questions like 'how should I explain this fund's recent drawdown to a nervous client'. The adviser then writes their own message to the client through the firm's messaging platform, which is archived and surveilled with a compliance lexicon. Compliance has noticed the assistant is not captured anywhere. What should the architect recommend?

options.A: Route adviser interactions with the assistant through the same capture and supervision pipeline as client messaging, since advice content is now being formed in a channel supervision cannot see.
options.B: Rely on the existing sent-message archive, because only communications that actually reach a client can constitute a communication with the public requiring supervision and archiving.
options.C: Disable the assistant for client-facing advisers and permit it only for back-office use, on the basis that generated content cannot be supervised to the required standard.
options.D: Add a disclosure to client messages stating that some content was drafted with AI assistance, which discharges the firm's supervision responsibility for the tool.

items.question: A manufacturer's in-house legal team wants a Claude assistant over its matter management system, whose corpus includes external counsel advice memos, litigation strategy notes and routine contract templates. The general counsel's concern is loss of legal privilege. The platform team's default design indexes the whole corpus into one vector store and emits full request and response traces to the company's shared observability platform, which the wider engineering organisation can query. What is the primary control?

options.A: Rely on the confidentiality obligations in the model provider's agreement and keep the single shared index, since the external disclosure risk is the one that threatens privilege.
options.B: Label every generated answer as privileged and confidential in a header, so the protection travels with the output regardless of who inside the company receives it.
options.C: Keep privileged material in a separately permissioned index with entitlements enforced at retrieval time, and exclude privileged payloads from the shared observability platform.
options.D: Exclude privileged documents from the index entirely and limit the assistant to contract templates, since any retrieval over privileged material creates an unacceptable waiver risk.

items.question: Under the EU AI Act, what distinguishes a practice in the prohibited tier from one in the high-risk tier?

options.A: It processes special categories of personal data and therefore requires an additional lawful condition before deployment.
options.B: It is treated as posing an unacceptable risk to fundamental rights, so it may not be placed on the market or used at all.
options.C: It operates without meaningful human oversight, and adding a qualified reviewer would move it down into the high-risk tier.
options.D: It is deployed by a public authority rather than a private organisation, which automatically raises the applicable tier.

items.question: A Finnish public employment service will deploy a third party's high-risk AI system, already placed on the EU market by its provider, to help caseworkers assess jobseeker support needs. The service is the deployer and is making no modification to the system or its intended purpose. Its programme board is allocating responsibilities. Which THREE responsibilities sit with the service as deployer? (Choose THREE.)

options.A: Drawing up the technical documentation that demonstrates the system meets the applicable requirements before it is put into service.
options.B: Using the system in line with the provider's instructions for use, including keeping operation within the stated intended purpose.
options.C: Assigning human oversight to individuals with the necessary competence, authority and organisational support to exercise it.
options.D: Carrying out the conformity assessment procedure for the system before it is placed on the market, and completing the associated declaration.
options.E: Retaining the logs the system automatically generates, to the extent those logs are under the service's control, for as long as its own obligations require.

items.question: An Irish health insurer has negotiated contractual commitments from its model provider that inputs will not be used to train models and will not be retained after the request completes. The audit committee asks the architect what, beyond the clause itself, gives the commitment operational force. Which TWO measures do that? (Choose TWO.)

options.A: Verifying periodically that the account, endpoints and features actually called sit inside the covered configuration, since the commitment attaches to a defined path.
options.B: Enabling client-side encryption of prompt payloads with keys the insurer holds, so the provider cannot read the content it is asked to process.
options.C: Requiring the vendor to publish a model card for each model version served to the insurer's account, covering evaluations and intended use.
options.D: Securing a right to independent assurance over the vendor's controls on the commitment, exercised on a recurring cadence rather than only at onboarding.
options.E: Extending the insurer's own request log retention so that any discrepancy with the vendor's retention behaviour can be reconciled line by line during a later review.

items.question: An Italian regional health service has completed a data protection impact assessment for a Claude-based symptom triage assistant that will direct callers to emergency, urgent or routine care. After every mitigation the team could identify, the assessment still records a high residual risk to individuals from incorrect urgency downgrades. The programme director wants to launch next month. What does the assessment's conclusion require?

options.A: Sign-off by the data protection officer, whose approval of the completed assessment is the authorisation for the programme to proceed to launch.
options.B: Consultation with the supervisory authority before the processing begins, because a high residual risk that mitigation cannot bring down is precisely the trigger for it.
options.C: Acceptance of the residual risk by the executive risk committee and recording it on the corporate risk register, which is the standard route for risk the organisation chooses to bear.
options.D: Proceeding to launch with the residual risk under monitoring by the programme board, provided the assessment is formally repeated at least annually.
